issues.description: Fields in class Lecture are declared with snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) in the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java), but the constructor, getters, setters and other methods in the same solution file use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The problem statement UML and task text also specify camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, ...). This mismatch makes the solution uncompilable (references to fields like this.lectureName do not exist) and will block students from using the provided solution or from understanding the intended attribute names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier names consistent. Preferred fix: rename the private fields in the solution to the camelCase names used elsewhere and in the UML: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; This aligns fields with the constructor, getters, setters, methods and the problem statement. Alternatively, update the constructor and all method references to use the snake_case field names, but keep naming consistent across the class and consistent with the UML to avoid confusing students and compilation errors.

issues.description: Concept: the Lecture attributes (lecture name and counts of different participant types). The problem statement names the attributes using camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. In the solution implementation the private fields are declared with snake_case identifiers: lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors, while the constructor, getters, setters and other methods reference the camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, etc.). This mismatch means the code references identifiers that are not declared, will cause compilation errors, and prevents students from clearly mapping the problem requirements to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute identifiers consistent with the problem statement and Java naming conventions. Rename the private fields in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. Ensure the constructor parameters, constructor body, all getters, setters, toString and other methods reference these same camelCase field names. Alternatively, if you prefer snake_case fields, update all references (constructor, getters, setters, toString) to use the declared snake_case names — but prefer the camelCase option to match the exercise text and standard Java style.
